ai.title: Fix setoutput tool tests by mocking agent templates
ai.summary: Replaced `assembleLocalAgentTemplates` calls with inline `testAgent` mocks in `run-agent-step-tools.test.ts`. Updated `agentType` params to match new mock IDs and removed unnecessary `as any` casts. Ensures `set_output` tool tests run deterministically without relying on real registry state.

eli5.text: The automated checks that verify the set_output tool works correctly were sometimes failing because they depended on the real set of available agents being in place. Now those checks use a fake, predictable agent configuration built right into the test, so they no longer rely on the actual system state. The tool tests now run reliably every time, producing the same result regardless of the current setup. You wouldn't see this directly, but it means the tests backing this tool are more stable.

ai.title: Refactor agent builder and add diff-reviewer examples
ai.summary: Consolidated `agent-builder` into base builder logic and added three `diff-reviewer` example agents (`.agents/examples/diff-reviewer-{1,2,3}.ts`) to demonstrate complexity levels. Updated `AgentConfig` type in `.agents/types/agent-config.d.ts` replacing `outputMode: 'json'` with `'structured_output'` and changing `toolResult` type from `ToolResult` to `string`. Removed `send_agent_message` from `superagent.ts` tools and added `spawn_agent_inline` to `ToolName` union in `.agents/types/tools.d.ts`. These changes standardize agent creation patterns and clarify output handling for sub-agents.

eli5.text: The system now includes three ready-made example assistants that show different ways to review code changes, from simple to more advanced. It also tidied up how assistant-building parts connect to each other and adjusted how assistants talk to one another behind the scenes. If you looked at the new examples, you'd see them guide an assistant through running a diff check and reading changed files; if you looked at the configuration files, you'd notice labels for output styles changed from one term to another and one messaging feature was taken away. These example assistants are available now as templates you can use or copy.

ai.title: Agent validation moves from WebSocket init to REST API route
ai.summary: Agent template validation shifted from backend WebSocket init to a new web REST endpoint `/api/agents/validate`. The CLI now triggers validation via `validateAgentConfigsIfAuthenticated` after loading local agents, replacing the previous `init-response` message payload. This decouples validation logic from the real-time connection, relying on `next-auth` sessions for authentication. Removed static agent template documentation and simplified file context assembly in `project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: Starting today (August 11, 2025), the assistant now checks your custom AI helper configurations through a regular web request instead of during its initial startup handshake. This means if you use tools like Codestream or Cursor to build custom agents, the validation of those configurations happens separately from establishing the main connection. You won't notice a difference in how quickly the assistant starts up, but behind the scenes it's now validating your agent templates through a dedicated check that authenticates using your session. The old method of embedding validation in the startup response has been removed, along with outdated documentation files that listed supported agent types.

ai.title: Agent validation endpoint drops auth, takes array
ai.summary: The /api/agents/validate endpoint no longer requires authentication and accepts an array of agent configs instead of a keyed object. The npm client passes Object.values(agentTemplates) and omits the session token cookie. The web route converts the array to a keyed object via Object.fromEntries before calling validateAgents. Affects npm-app/src/client.ts, npm-app/src/utils/agent-validation.ts, web/src/app/api/agents/validate/route.ts.

eli5.text: Starting today, the tool no longer checks if you are logged in before it validates your agent configurations. You can now send a list of agent configurations directly to the validation endpoint instead of packaging them inside a named object, and the web route automatically converts that list back into a named structure before processing. If you look, you would notice that the validation step runs the same way on its own, without needing your session token or login cookie, and the data it accepts has flattened from a key-value map to a simple array of configurations.

ai.title: Add prompt-error action for WebSocket errors
ai.summary: Introduced `prompt-error` server action to standardize error reporting for prompt executions. Replaced manual `response-chunk` and `prompt-response` error assembly with dedicated typed actions in `backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts` and `websocket-action.ts`. Updated `ClientAction` and `ServerAction` types to generic discriminated unions in `common/src/actions.ts`. CLI client `npm-app/src/client.ts` now subscribes to both `action-error` and `prompt-error` to handle insufficient credits and other failures.

eli5.text: When the system runs your request and something goes wrong because your organization doesn't have enough credit, the client tool now receives a clearer error message that tells you exactly which request failed and why. The client tool will show you the same clear message whether the failure is a general problem or specific to a single prompt, so you won't have to guess which request ran out of credit.

ai.title: Move agent config validation to CLI startup
ai.summary: Removed async validation from `client.ts` initialization and moved it to `index.ts` CLI startup. Validation now triggers immediately after `loadLocalAgents` resolves, ensuring local templates are checked before WebSocket connection or UI display. This shift decouples validation from the core client lifecycle, restricting it to the CLI entry point. Files changed: `npm-app/src/client.ts`, `npm-app/src/index.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant starts up, it now checks your templates right away instead of waiting until later. You won't see any visible change in how the assistant behaves, but the internal checks happen earlier to catch template problems before the assistant connects or shows its first screen.

ai.title: thinkdeeply no longer forces next agent step
ai.summary: Added TOOLS_WHICH_WONT_FORCE_NEXT_STEP constant in common/src/tools/constants.ts to exclude think_deeply from forcing continuation. Updated backend/src/run-agent-step.ts to calculate shouldEndTurn by filtering out these non-forcing tools from toolCalls and toolResults checks. This prevents the agent from unnecessarily looping when only think_deeply is called without other actionable tools.

eli5.text: If the AI assistant only used its 'think deeply' tool during a turn, it would sometimes keep going in a loop even though there was nothing left to do. Now, that thinking-only tool is ignored when deciding whether the assistant should stop and hand control back, so a turn that consists solely of internal reasoning ends cleanly instead of lingering. You would notice this when the assistant wraps up a step that was purely analytical rather than continuing to call tools. The change is live today.

ai.title: Add newlines before terminal command display
ai.summary: Two blank lines added via `console.log()` before printing the green `displayDir > command` string in `runCommandChildProcess`. This compensates for models that omit newlines in their output. Scope limited to `npm-app/src/terminal/run-command.ts`.

eli5.text: When you run a command in the terminal, the assistant's reply and the command that gets executed are printed out. Some newer AI models finish their response without pressing Enter, so the printed command would get jammed up against the model's last line of text. Now, the system adds two blank lines before showing the command, so everything lines up neatly on its own lines. You'd notice the extra spacing when watching the terminal run commands, making the output easier to read. This is live today and applies to anyone running commands through the terminal.

ai.title: Adjust agent step logging
ai.summary: Reorders fields and updates included data in `logger.debug` calls within `run-agent-step.ts`. The 'Start' log now includes `iteration`, `model`, and `duration` earlier, while the 'End' log drops `fullResponseChunks` and `agentTemplate` in favor of `shouldEndTurn` and `finalMessageHistoryWithToolResults`. This change is scoped to the backend agent execution loop. No user-facing behavior or API changes occur.

eli5.text: The system's behind-the-scenes logging, used by developers to troubleshoot the agent's brain, was reorganized. The 'Start' log now lists the step number, model name, and elapsed time earlier in the list, while the 'End' log removed the old raw response chunks and agent template fields in favor of cleaner, more relevant data like the final message history. No users notice this directly; it simply makes the logs easier to read for whoever is debugging the agent later.

ai.summary: The backend now sends a 'prompt-error' action with validation messages from assembleLocalAgentTemplates on every prompt. This ensures invalid agent configs are reported immediately. The change affects backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant something, it now checks your agent settings right away and sends back an error message immediately if those settings are invalid, instead of letting the problem hide until later. If you looked, you'd see a new error notification appear with each prompt when your configuration has problems. This affects internal tooling used by developers building and testing agents, and the change is live as of today.

ai.summary: The `ModelName` union in `common/src/util/types/agent-config.d.ts` now explicitly lists recommended models, replacing the generic 'all models' comment. Added entries include `openai/gpt-5` variants, `anthropic/claude-opus-4.1`, `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, `qwen/qwen3-coder`, `deepseek/deepseek-chat-v3-0324`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2`, and `z-ai/glm-4.5`. Removed outdated models like `anthropic/claude-3.5-haiku-20241022` and `openai/gpt-4o-2024-11-20`. The `(string & {})` fallback remains, allowing any OpenRouter model ID.

eli5.text: The set of AI brains your assistant can pick from has been refreshed: newer recommended models like GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, and Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite are now explicitly suggested, while older ones such as GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Haiku have been dropped. If you open the model picker when configuring an assistant, you'll see these current options right up front instead of a comment saying every model works; you can still type in any other model supported by OpenRouter. This took effect on 2025-08-11 and only affects people building or customizing agents in this software.

ai.title: Refactor WebSocket action types to generic ClientAction
ai.summary: Replaced verbose `Extract<ClientAction, { type: T }>` and `Extract<ServerAction, { type: T }>` patterns with generic type parameters `ClientAction<T>` and `ServerAction<T>` across the WebSocket layer. This simplifies type inference and reduces boilerplate in action handlers, middleware, and client subscriptions. Changes span `backend/src/websockets`, `common/src/websockets`, `npm-app/src/client.ts`, and `sdk/src`. The refactor is purely internal, preserving runtime behavior while improving type ergonomics.

ai.title: Rename AgentState spawnableAgents to subagents
ai.summary: Renamed `spawnableAgents` field to `subagents` in `AgentStateSchema` and related handlers. This aligns internal state naming with the concept of nested agent execution. Updated `common/src/types/session-state.ts`, `backend/src/tools/handlers/tool/spawn-*.ts`, and `common/src/util/types/agent-config.d.ts`. The `agent-config.d.ts` comment now explicitly requires fully qualified IDs (publisher/version) or local file IDs for spawning.

eli5.text: The system now keeps track of helper assistants inside another assistant using a clearer name, so when one assistant calls on smaller specialist assistants to help with your request, they're stored under 'subagents' instead of the old 'spawnableAgents'. If you looked at how the system organizes things internally, you would see this consistent naming and a more explicit rule telling developers that any assistant they want the main assistant to be able to call on must be referenced by its full name including publisher and version, or by a local file name. This change is live today and affects how nested assistants are tracked and spawned.
